expeditions.name: Tyresta
expeditions.terrain: Old pine forest, granite ridges, the area burnt in 1999, boardwalks over bogs
expeditions.climate: Early March: −4 to +3 °C, frozen lakes, 11 hours of daylight
expeditions.note: A day hike through Tyresta National Park, one hour from central Stockholm by bus. Old pine forest, granite ridges and quiet lakes, and a good first trip with the club.
log: Meeting point at Gullmarsplan; bus 834 towards Tyresta.
Start at Tyresta village, by the national park entrance.
Lunch break on the rocks above Årsjön.
Back at the village after 16 km.

gallery: On the trail through the spruce forest.

expeditions.name: Kebnekaise
expeditions.terrain: Moraine, scree, the Vierranvárri shoulder, a snow ridge to the top
expeditions.transport: Night train to Kiruna, bus to Nikkaluokta, 19 km on foot to the mountain station
expeditions.climate: Late August: 0 to +12 °C at the station, below zero on the summit ridge, wind
expeditions.note: Four days to Sweden’s highest mountain, with the summit day on the western route from the Kebnekaise mountain station.
log: Departure from the Kebnekaise mountain station (690 m).
Vierranvárri (1,711 m) and the first view of the summit ridge.
Back at the mountain station after 18 km and 1,900 m of ascent.

gallery: The last ridge to the top.

expeditions.name: Stockholm Archipelago
expeditions.terrain: Ice-polished granite shore, heath, pine, the old pilot station
expeditions.transport: Commuter train to Nynäshamn, bus to Ankarudden, boat to Öja
expeditions.note: A two-day coastal hike on Öja (Landsort), the southernmost island of the Stockholm archipelago, with a night at the old pilot station by Sweden’s oldest lighthouse.
log: Arrival on Öja and a walk around the island.
Overnight stay at the pilot station.
Boat back to the mainland after 11 km.

expeditions.name: Abisko
expeditions.terrain: Birch forest, the Abisko canyon, open fell, the Njullá ridge
expeditions.transport: Night train from Stockholm Central to Abisko Turiststation, about 17 hours
expeditions.climate: Mid-October: −5 to +4 °C, the first snow on the mountains, about nine hours of daylight, northern lights on clear nights
expeditions.cost: Train, huts and food at cost, listed when registration closes
expeditions.leaders: Two club trip leaders; a certified guide for the Njullá ridge
expeditions.note: Three days in Abisko National Park in October: birch forest, the Abisko valley and the Njullá ridge, with the first snow on the mountains.

itinerary.title: Up the Abisko valley
itinerary.text: We arrive on the morning train, walk through the Abisko canyon and follow Kungsleden along the river to the Abiskojaure mountain hut.

itinerary.title: Across the open fell
itinerary.text: We leave the marked trail and cross the open fell above the tree line. We stay in a hut or in tents, depending on the conditions.

itinerary.title: Njullá and the journey home
itinerary.text: With a certified guide we climb the Njullá ridge (1,169 m), then walk down to Abisko for the evening train to Stockholm.

packing: Hat, buff, two pairs of gloves
Map and compass, the club brings the rest

gallery: Lapporten from the frozen shore of Torneträsk, midwinter.

expeditions.name: Sarek
expeditions.terrain: No marked trails or huts: frozen valleys and mountain passes on skis
expeditions.transport: Night train to Gällivare, bus to Kvikkjokk, then on ski
expeditions.climate: March: −20 to −2 °C, long light, storms that last days
expeditions.leaders: Two certified mountain leaders; ski touring experience required
expeditions.note: A week-long ski tour through Sarek National Park in March, with tents and pulks. For members who have joined a winter trip with the club before.

activities.name: Hiking
activities.text: Day hikes on trails such as Sörmlandsleden and Roslagsleden, within an hour of Stockholm. Regular trips throughout the year.

activities.name: Climbing
activities.equipment: Harness and shoes, lent by the club
activities.text: Indoor climbing during the darker months and outdoor climbing on granite south of Stockholm from May. Belay courses are offered for beginners.

activities.name: Alpine
activities.text: Glacier travel and summit trips in the Swedish mountains, always led by certified mountain guides, with at most six people per rope team.

activities.name: Winter
activities.text: Snowshoeing, ski touring and walks on frozen lakes during the winter months.

activities.name: Expeditions
activities.text: Multi-day trips to the Swedish mountains, travelling by night train and staying in mountain huts or tents. Two to three trips a year.
